newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: FOCUS-Daewoo gets 40 pct of Kazakhtelekom monopoly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Daewoo gets 40 pct of Kazakhtelekom monopoly.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Corp has bought a 40 percent stake in Kazakhstan telecoms monopoly Kazakhtelekom for $1.37 billion, government and Daewoo officials said Monday.
"On May 31 Kazakhstan's government and Daewoo Corporation signed a contract... The value of the deal is $1.37 billion," A government press release said.
"Daewoo has bought a 40 percent stake," Kazakhtelekom Chairman Serik Burkitbayev told a news conference.
"We are very delighted to become the strategic partner of Kazakhtelekom in its modernisation and expansion programme," said Kim Choong-Se, Executive Vice President of Daewoo Telecom Services Group.

Transport and Communications Minister Yuri Lavrinenko said the deal -- preceded by an April framework agreement with Daewoo after it won a tender to negotiate a contract -- stipulated that the Korean partner must invest about $1 billion in Kazakhtelekom by the year 2000.
Daewoo will also pay the government a bonus of $100 million and pay off by the year 2000 Kazakhtelekom's debt of 390 million marks to German investment agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau.
"If Kazakhtelekom was not burdened with obligations to German creditors... the task of finding a strategic partner would not have been so tough," Burkitbayev said.
He said that last year Kazakhtelekom, which employs 50,000 workers, had a pre-tax profit of $70 million but had to pay $62 million as interest for the German loan.
Daewoo has pledged to increase the Central Asian state's telecoms network to 3.3 million lines from today's 2.3 million and modernise Kazakhtelekom's equipment.

Burkitbayev said that with Daewoo's help Kazakhstan -- a resource-rich country, five times the size of France but with a population of just 16.7 million -- was planning to become a communications hub linking Europe and Asia.
"The advent of this world-famous company allows us to set such ambitious goals," he said.

Daewoo beat South Korea's Hanwha, Germany's Siemens AG, Alcatel Alsthom SA unit Alcatel Sel AG, Malaysia's Usaha Tegas Sdn Bnd and British Virgin Islands registered Kaztel Investment Group in the tender.
Last year Kazakhstan's government signed a framework agreement with Germany's Deutsche Telekom for management control and a 49 percent stake of Kazakhtelekom but the deal fell through in December.
"The deal with Daewoo is much more advantageous than with Deutsche Telekom," said Eduard Utepov, head of the finance ministry's privatisation department.
"Currently Kazakhtelekom has an annual revenue of around $500 million. It is expected that by the year 2000... the company's revenues will reach $1 billion," the press release said.

Burkitbayev said that by the end of this year Kazakhtelekom would undertake necessary listing procedures on the domestic stock market and did not rule out the possiblity of trading its shares on foreign markets over the next two or three years.
